sections.title: Ethical, Legal and Social Implications of Neuroscience
sections.description: Neuroscience increasingly poses ethical issues relevant to everyday life, from students taking Adderall as a study aid to the use of brain scans to argue for clemency in criminal court proceedings. These and many other practices evoke moral judgments and may soon become subject to legislation, regulation and other forms of policy. Society needs to address these issues with an understanding of the science and its likely impact, as well as the ability to go beyond gut level reactions to analyze the ethical issues more thoughtfully. This seminar will build on students’ introductory level knowledge of neuroscience and help them develop the skills to analyze and discuss the ethical implications of the science. They will thus be positioned to guide legal and policy discussions about neuroscience in society.
